html:
The Northern Territory was the vast tropical north of central Australia, which Britain gave to the colony of South Australia to govern in 1863. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. In 1911 it passed to the federal government of Australia.

South Australia hoped to make it pay. A first settlement at Escape Cliffs failed, and in 1869 a survey party laid out Palmerston, later renamed Darwin, on Port Darwin. In 1872 the Overland Telegraph Line reached it from Adelaide and joined an undersea cable to Java, tying Australia to London by telegraph.

Gold was found near Pine Creek while the line was being built, and Chinese miners and workers soon outnumbered Europeans in the Top End. Cattle stations spread over the grasslands, and a railway inland from Darwin began in the 1880s. But the territory never paid its way, and its white population stayed tiny.

Most people were Aboriginal, such as the Yolngu and the Yanyuwa, and much of the land was still theirs in practice. The Makassan trepang visits to the coast, centuries old, were ended by South Australia in 1906.
